text.p: Italian debt markets streaked ahead on the latest lap of their bull run in late trade, with new contract highs and fresh records on the Italy-Germany yield spread becoming almost commonplace.

The cash February 2007 Btp spread over the July 2007 Bund fell to its latest record low of 111 basis points in the closing moments, straight from 114 previously. The price was 70 basis points up at 100.40 and the actual yield 6.79 percent.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi proved to be not far wrong when he said earlier in the day the spread could go lower. At the time of his comments it was at its then record of 116.
Brokers tended to agree with Ciampi: "On the spread we could reach 110 soon and probably 100 further on," one said.

"There's no reason for the moment to sell the BTP against the Bund. There are some uncertainties but the market is not paying attention to potential problems of the welfare reforms under discussion," the broker added.
The September Btp futures contract on LIFFE hit yet another record peak of 134.65 and was trading just below that, 61 basis points up on the day at 134.61 at 1523 GMT.
"We need a pullback," a broker said. Another added: "Its overbought but that doesn't necessarily mean a correction."

Bank of Italy lira repo operations earlier provided a little food for thought when the minimum rate fell to a historic low of 6.26 percent. Monetary sources discounted the idea this might be a signal of lower official rates in the offing from the central bank, saying instead the rate fell due to technical reasons.
On the less rosy front, Italian unemployment also hit a new high, with joblessness rising to 12.5 percent in April against 12.4 percent in January and 12.3 percent in the same month last year.
